chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Husayn Al-Farsi, from Suleiman ibn Ja'far, from Ismail ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The water which the sun warms up, do not perform Wudu with it, nor perform Ghusl with it, nor knead with it, for it causes leprosy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using sun-warmed water for ritual ablution and bathing in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines a legal ruling regarding the water heated by the sun (sun-warmed water), prohibiting its use for ritual purification (Wudu and Ghusl) and kneading dough due to its tendency to cause leprosy (Al-Baras). In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted through the lens of 'illat' (effective cause), where the sun's heating process alters the water's purity or health properties, linking physical hygiene with spiritual ritual validity. The prohibition highlights the interconnection between bodily health and ritual cleanliness in Shia fiqh.
